summary: Tested Barangay Management System (backend + frontend). Auth, Dashboard, Residents list/create/search all work. CRITICAL bug: residents are inserted with only MongoDB _id; no application 'id' field is generated. As a result, GET /api/residents/{id}, PUT, DELETE, and POST /api/document-requests (which validates resident by 'id') all return 404. This breaks the entire Documents workflow (create request -> approve -> download PDF) and resident edit/delete from UI.

critical.issue: Resident document is not assigned an 'id' field on creation. Insert uses Mongo _id only, but response returns str(result.inserted_id) as 'id'. Subsequent queries use {'id': resident_id} -> 404 always.
Always returns 404 due to missing 'id' field in stored docs.
Always returns 404 (same root cause). UI delete button is non-functional.
Resident lookup fails -> 404 'Resident not found'. Blocks entire document workflow.

minor.issue: Projection excludes _id but resident objects also have no 'id' field, so frontend cannot reference individual residents by id (delete/edit broken end-to-end).

Will always fail because backend returns 404 (id mismatch bug above).

integration_issues.issue: Cannot create any document request because resident_id never matches in DB.

rca of the issue: Root cause: server.py POST /api/residents inserts resident_doc which contains no 'id' key. After insert, code sets resident_doc['id'] = str(result.inserted_id) ONLY on the in-memory dict returned to client; the DB document has only Mongo _id. All later endpoints (GET/PUT/DELETE/{resident_id} and POST /document-requests) look up by {'id': resident_id} which never matches. Fix: add resident_doc['id'] = secrets.token_urlsafe(16) (or str(ObjectId())) before db.residents.insert_one(resident_doc). Reproduction: POST /api/residents then GET /api/residents/{returned_id} -> 404.
